chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said:

When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in Kufa during the time of Abu al-Abbas, he came riding his mount in his travel clothes until he stopped at the bridge of Kufa. Then he said to his servant, 'Give me water.' He took a potter's bowl, scooped water from it, and gave it to him to drink. He drank the water while it flowed over his beard and clothes. Then he asked for more, and he gave him more; he asked again, and he gave him more. He praised Allah, then said, 'A river, how great is its blessing! Indeed, every day seven drops from Paradise fall into it. If people knew what blessing is in it, they would pitch their tents on its banks. And if it were not for the sinners entering it, no one with an ailment would immerse himself in it without being cured.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical blessings of the Euphrates River according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual merit of the Euphrates (Al-Furat) in Kufa, a key site for Shia devotional practices. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the river's dual nature: it is a source of divine healing and heavenly blessing, yet its purity is slightly mitigated by the presence of sinners, illustrating the concept of *khata'at* (minor impurities/sins) affecting sacred spaces. This hadith is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence and theology to justify the recommendation of drinking and performing ablution with Euphrates water.
